name: Supabase
summary: A backend platform that composes PostgreSQL with generated APIs, authentication, row-level security, realtime services, storage, and edge execution.

features.name: Database-centered platform composition
features.description: PostgreSQL is the core system and surrounding services expose APIs, authentication, realtime behavior, storage, and management capabilities around it.
benefits: Reuses PostgreSQL semantics, extensions, and ecosystem
costs: The platform inherits operational and conceptual complexity from the database-centered design

features.name: Database-enforced access control
features.description: Authentication and API access are integrated with PostgreSQL row-level security policies.
benefits: Centralizes fine-grained data authorization near the data
costs: Authorization behavior depends on correct database policy design and context propagation

mathematical_views.model: Composed service graph with a shared authority
mathematical_views.question: How do independently deployable services expose a coherent backend contract?
assumptions: PostgreSQL remains the authoritative data system for the platform
Service boundaries preserve the relevant database security context

mathematical_views.question: How can data access be modeled as queries filtered by row-level authorization predicates?
assumptions: Policies are evaluated by PostgreSQL for the relevant operation

benefits: Fast path from schema to application-facing capabilities
costs: The database becomes a central architectural dependency and governance boundary

benefits: Consistent authorization across generated and direct database access
costs: Policy debugging and testing become part of database engineering

evidence.title: Supabase Architecture
evidence.notes: Primary documentation listing the platform components and their relationships.

relations.notes: Supabase assembles APIs, authentication, realtime, storage, and management services around PostgreSQL as its core system; this records documented composition, not historical influence or implementation equivalence.
